title: LLM paper snapshots + quick experiment ideas
content:
Purpose: quickfire one-paragraph snapshots of recent papers I want to test/remember, plus 1–2 tiny experiment ideas per paper that are realistic on Redwood infra. Not a polished lit review — more like a lab notebook for next sprint.

1) "Efficient Latent Caches for Long Context" (arXiv 2601.01234) — quick take:
- Core idea: store compact latent summaries (projected KV) for long segments and stitch them back into decoding for long-range context without repeatedly passing full token streams. Empirical claim: ~4x memory reduction with <2% perf loss on longform tasks.
- Why I care: could be a middle ground between full KV caching and retrieval-style retrievals for customers with multi-hour sessions. Lower memory = cheaper Dedicated pods.
- Small experiment: implement a toy projection layer on top of our existing KV cache that downsamples cached keys by factor 4 (PCA-like linear proj). Run on the wiki-long dataset (synth transcript) with our existing 8k/64k model variants. Measure perplexity, per-token latency, and peak GPU memory. Ticket: GH#infra-experiments/kv-proj-test.
- Risks: projection might break fast attention kernels; need to validate kernel compatibility.

2) "Quantization Stability: Dynamic Range Preserving Methods" — quick take:
- Core idea: dynamic-range-aware clipping before quantization + tiny per-layer calibration passes yields much more stable generation across seeds.
- Why: low-bit quantization is attractive for Dedicated and Private. Stability issues are what stops us from recommending aggressive 4-bit configs in Optimize.
- Tiny experiment: run 4-bit GPT-like quant on a small 7B open model with and without dynamic clipping. Generate 100 prompts from our eval set (customer prompt set anonymized) and compute token-level divergence + downstream BLEU-like metric for instruction tasks. If divergence < 6% and sample quality preserved, flag as candidate for Optimize suggestions. Link to mock script: /scripts/quant-eval/quick-dynclip.sh (prototype).

3) "Adaptive Batching by Sequence Shape" (conference slide set I skimmed) — quick take:
- Core idea: scheduler groups requests by expected decode length and memory footprint (shape), allowing more aggressive batching of short sequences while preserving latency for long ones.
- Why: should reduce queuing latency tail while preserving throughput — aligns with our smart routing philosophy.
- Experiment idea: in Dedicated dev pool, enable a scheduler that glimpses first token and puts into short/long queue (heuristic). Compare 99th percentile latency and average tokens/sec for mixed workload (chat + summarization). Use traces from Feb traffic (anonymized). If promising, add feature flag behind canary rollout in console.

4) "KV Sharding for Heterogeneous GPUs" (workshop paper) — quick take:
- Core idea: split KV by time ranges and route shards to GPUs with different memory/compute; reconstruction on decode. Good when customer Dedicated clusters are mixed generation (A100 + H100?).
- Why: we get customers asking about incremental add-on GPUs to clusters; could avoid rebalancing.
- Mini-probe: simulate two-GPU cluster with different memory caps on our local rust runtime (use unit tests that simulate memory limits). Measure additional mem copy overhead and latency delta for 2,4,8k contexts. If overhead < 10% and memory wins are big, add to design doc for Dedicated autoscaling.

5) "Mixture-of-KVs: Routing for Conditional Memory" — quick take:
- Idea: make multiple small KV banks specialized by topic/style and route queries to one or two most-likely banks. Akin to MoE but for memory retrieval.
- Why: might reduce retrieval noise in RAG-like setups and allow smaller bank sizes (cheaper storage and faster lookup).
- Scratch experiment: prototype offline clustering on transcripts (k=8), build per-cluster KV banks (dense vectors -> ANN). Evaluate retrieval precision@k and hallucination rate on a Q/A benchmark. If precision gains > 8% at same latency, it's worth a deeper pass.

Practical notes / to-do (short):
- Prioritize the latent-cache projection experiment this sprint. Ask SRE for a 2-node dev Dedicated pool (ticket JIRA-INF-892).
- Add a small benchmark harness: 100 prompts x 3 seeds x configs {baseline, proj-4x} -> record PT, memory, perplexity. Keep scripts idempotent.
- Coordinate with Talia for eval set selection (avoid customer PII).
- Check GH PR infra/pull/1284 for recent kernel changes that might affect low-bit projection matrix ops.

Quick reminders to self:
- Keep experiment reproducible: save docker hash, exact model commit, and seed.
- Write short draft for Optimize playbook if projection looks good (one-pager: TLDR, perf, SLO impact, recommended configs).
- If quant experiment shows improved stability, talk to Solutions Eng about a beta with 2 customers on Dedicated.

Loose hypotheses (for future tests):
- H1: Projected KV caches will preserve >98% of answer relevance for segments shorter than 2k tokens.
- H2: Dynamic clipping at calibration reduces generation variance by >25% relative to standard static quant.
- H3: Simple two-queue scheduler (short/long) will cut 95th pct latency by ~30% for mixed chat+long workload without reducing throughput.

Offhand links / reading queue (short list):
- arXiv:2601.01234 (latent caches)
- quant stability notes (internal GH gist) -> linked_artifacts above
- slides: adaptive-batching-ops-ICLR (Slack #infra-research)

End notes: this doc = living snapshots. Next update will be after the projection prototype run (ETA: 2026-04-20). If anything looks promising, will convert into a proper PRD and a small slate in the Optimize roadmap.

-- Brio
